title: Microsoft's MAI-DxO orchestrates a panel of agents to diagnose NEJM cases
summary: Microsoft AI introduced MAI-DxO, a model-agnostic orchestrator that turns a language model into a virtual panel of clinicians which asks follow-up questions, orders (virtual) tests or delivers a diagnosis, and runs a cost check and verifies its own reasoning before deciding whether to proceed. On the Sequential Diagnosis Benchmark built from 304 recent NEJM cases it solved 85.5% of cases when paired with OpenAI's o3, against a mean of 20% for 21 practising US and UK physicians working without references, at lower testing cost; Microsoft states the system is a research demonstration that is not yet approved for clinical use and would only be approved after rigorous safety testing, clinical validation and regulatory reviews.

actors.model: OpenAI o3 (orchestrated by MAI-DxO; GPT, Llama, Claude, Gemini, Grok and DeepSeek also tested)
